sector: Subscription strength training app with a coached movement library, sold direct to home gym subscribers.
founded_place_size: Providence, Rhode Island; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
about: Anvil and Oak Strength is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Providence, Rhode Island, and this commission covers phase 2: coached movement video library.
audience: Subscribers aged 30 to 52 with a home or garage gym, already lifting and paying for instruction rather than motivation. They can tell a coach from a cheerleader and buy the difference.
price_positioning: 49 dollars a month, coached strength, extended a quarter at a time. Positioned as a working coach's studio: clearly above a 9 dollar mass fitness app and deliberately clear of a clinical or rehabilitation register.
typography: Display: a sturdy, slightly condensed slab or grotesque with real weight and confidence. Text: a plain, legible humanist sans. The cue list is the hardest role, instruction read while someone is under a bar, so it favours clarity over character. No gym chain italics and no clinical thin weights.
voice: Direct, instructional and calm. Speaks like a coach giving a cue, not a brand selling one. Example line: 'Brace, hinge, drive through the floor. That is the whole lift.'
brand_assets_status: The wordmark and the in house certification seal survive only as stitching on a canvas gym bag patch, held now as one handheld photograph. Both have to be recovered from that photograph as artwork before they can go on the cards and the library sheet. The seal is a compound ring lockup, type set around a central anvil glyph inside a ruled ring. There is no vector file, no colour spec and no prior guideline.
values: Competence and honesty: real bodies doing real work, taught by people who actually lift.
